name: Pattern Monster
tagline: 460 seamless SVG patterns you recolour in-browser and copy as SVG or CSS
description: Pattern Monster is a browser pattern generator that ships 460 pre-drawn, seamlessly tiling SVG patterns across 85 families — waves, chevrons, herringbone, hexagons, scales, plaid, Memphis, Egyptian, Japanese, Chinese, African and seasonal sets. Each pattern exposes stroke width, spacing, rotation, scale and up to five colour stops, and the result can be copied as raw SVG, as a CSS background-image data URI, or downloaded as SVG or PNG. It is a SvelteKit app by Naveen CS; the free tier covers the whole library, and a separate Pro tier lives at pro.pattern.monster. Useful for page backgrounds, section dividers, empty-state art, packaging and apparel.

pricing_detail: Core generator is free with no signup. A separate Pro product exists at pro.pattern.monster/pricing (Paddle-backed), but the pricing page renders client-side only and the exact tiers could not be read.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a page needs a non-photographic background texture and you do not want another dependency — the output is a self-contained SVG or a CSS background-image data URI, so it drops into Tailwind, plain CSS or a React style prop with zero install. Deep-link straight to https://pattern.monster/<slug> (for example /waves-1, /herringbone-3, /memphis-pattern-4) instead of trying to browse; the homepage is a SvelteKit shell that a plain fetch renders as 'undefined'. Set opacity low and match the pattern stroke to a CSS variable, and check the tile size — a 120x80 tile that looks fine on a hero will visibly repeat inside a small card.
why_it_matters: It is the largest free library of parametric, genuinely seamless SVG patterns on the web, and the output format — inline SVG or a CSS data URI — is the one format that survives every framework and build tool.
notable_for: copy as SVG or CSS data URI
up to 5 colour stops per pattern

name: Recent
tagline: Daily-curated feed of websites, OG images, app icons, tools and agent skills
description: Recent is a curated design-inspiration index run by @senyil that took over from Godly, the website gallery it explicitly replaces. It splits into five galleries — a mixed Design feed, Websites, OG Images, App Screenshots and App Icons — plus three directories: Tools (with negotiated discount codes), Skills (installable Claude/agent design skills ranked by install count) and a paid Jobs board. Founded in 2023 as a collection of design work posted on X, it was relaunched in 2026 with a broader remit and now claims 250k+ monthly visitors and 25k+ newsletter subscribers.
pricing_detail: Free to browse; optional account. Job postings cost $149. Sponsorship sold separately via /sponsor. Tool listings carry affiliate discount codes (e.g. RECENT25 for Framer, RECENT20 for Interface Craft).
agent_guidance: Use this as the human-taste layer before you generate a marketing page — pull the Websites categories (AI, Agency, Portfolio, SaaS, Ecommerce, Startup, Product, Technology, Finance, Food & Drink, Music, Art, Photography, Architecture, Health, Education, Entertainment, Web3, Crypto, Editorial, Personal) to find a directionally right reference, then describe it rather than copying it. /skills is the most agent-relevant page: it indexes installable design skills such as anthropics/canvas-design, vercel-labs/web-design-guidelines and pbakaus/polish with live install counts, so it doubles as a discovery feed for your own tooling. Note that the site 403s a bare fetch and every gallery is screenshot-only — send a normal browser User-Agent, and expect no machine-readable metadata about the sites it features.
why_it_matters: It absorbed Godly's role as the default website-inspiration gallery and then went wider — OG images, iOS icons and App Store screenshots are all under-served categories, and the Skills directory is the only curated index of design-focused agent skills.
notable_for: OG image and App Store screenshot galleries
curated index of agent design skills

name: Adalat AI
tagline: Framer-built civic-tech site: stats-led hero, impact page, 37-role careers hub
description: Adalat AI is an Indian justice-technology nonprofit building courtroom transcription, case workflow and record digitisation for state judiciaries, and its site is indexed here as a UI reference rather than as a product you install. It is a Framer site with an unusually complete information architecture for a mission-driven org: a stats-heavy home page, /products, /impact, /about-us, /recognition, a full /security disclosure page (data residency, client-side encryption, no third-party API calls), an engineering blog with real ASR write-ups, and a /careers hub with 37 open roles across engineering, ML, legal and per-state project management. The /whatsapp-helpline page is a separate product landing built around a Claude-powered case-status bot.
agent_guidance: Pull this up when you are laying out a mission-driven or public-sector product site and need a structure that is not the usual SaaS hero-features-pricing template — the pattern here is problem statistics first, then impact numbers, then judge testimonials, then partners, with pricing replaced by a donate/partner call to action. The /security page is the most reusable piece: it is a clean template for a trust page (data residency, encryption, compliance, FAQ) that most B2G and enterprise products need and few do well. Do not try to scrape the rendered DOM — it is a Framer client-rendered site; fetch https://framerusercontent.com/sites/1cuDXVuo1TZuhckGptAiuq/searchIndex-itSpqjiiKHRa.json instead, which returns every page's title and heading tree as JSON.
why_it_matters: A rare, well-structured example of civic-tech and nonprofit information architecture — trust page, impact page and a 37-role careers hub — in an index otherwise dominated by SaaS marketing sites.
notable_for: stat-led problem framing on the hero

name: ASCII Magic
tagline: Client-side image and video stylizer: 15 art styles, 4x export, no signup
description: ASCII Magic turns any photo or video into one of 15 render styles — Characters, Block, Dots, Lines, Diagonal, Cross, Diamond, Mixed, Pixel Art, LEGO, Mosaic, Voxel Cubes, Disco, Dither and Glitch, plus a Braille renderer — with 15 stackable post-effects (CRT curve, scanlines, chromatic aberration, bloom, character glow, film grain, film dust, halftone, RGB split, vignette and more). Everything renders locally on HTML5 Canvas, so nothing uploads; input accepts JPG/PNG/WebP/GIF/MP4/MOV/WebM and output is PNG (with alpha), JPG, animated GIF or H.264 MP4 at up to 4x source resolution, never watermarked. The Dither style alone carries 11 algorithms and 16 palettes (1-bit, Game Boy, C64, NES, PICO-8, CGA, risograph). Free with no account, built by Kailash.

pricing_detail: Free forever — no signup, no watermark, no export limit, no ads, no Pro tier. Funded personally by the creator. Exports are cleared for commercial use; you only need rights to the source media.
agent_guidance: Reach for this when a hero, wallpaper or video intro needs a hand-made retro texture and a generic AI image would look generic — dither, halftone and voxel treatments of a real photo read as craft in a way Midjourney output does not. The key affordance for you is the recipe URL: state is delta-encoded base64 in ?r=<code> or ?recipe=<name>, so you can hand a user a deep link that opens the editor with the exact look pre-applied, and https://www.ascii-magic.com/context.md is a maintained product brief written to be pasted into an LLM — read that instead of scraping the marketing page. Watch the limits: no SVG or PDF export, video exports are silent and capped at 150 MB input, and images above 25 MP are rejected.
why_it_matters: It is a genuinely deep single-purpose tool — 15 styles, 11 dither algorithms, 16 palettes, video support, transparent PNG, 4x export — given away free with no account, and it publishes a context.md for agents, which almost no design tool does.
notable_for: video in, MP4 or GIF out

name: Hard Launch
tagline: One-line Framer site for a founder launch outfit; almost no readable content
description: Hard Launch is Jacky Huang's launch and storytelling outfit for early-stage founders, positioned as 'working with founders you'd want to root for'. The public site is deliberately minimal: five routes (/, /collab, /launch, /archive, /mofnts) whose entire indexed copy is 'HARD LAUNCH' and 'We all want to root for someone', plus a wall of outbound links to LinkedIn and X posts from companies it has worked with (Spur, Metis, Osmosis, Haize Labs). name: Switzer
tagline: Free neo-grotesque from ITF: 9 weights, matching italics, variable, 135 languages
description: Switzer is a Latin neo-grotesque by Jerémie Hornus for the Indian Type Foundry, released free on Fontshare in April 2021 (originally issued as Volkart in 2015). It ships 18 static styles — Thin through Black with a matching italic for each — plus two variable files (upright and italic, wght axis 100-900), covering 135 languages and carrying aalt, frac, liga, locl, ordn, salt and sups OpenType features. It is currently at version 1.2. Distributed under the ITF Free Font License, free for personal and commercial work in desktop, web and app contexts.
pricing_detail: Free. ITF Free Font License (license_type: itf_ffl) — personal and commercial use permitted; ITF retains copyright and trademark.
agent_guidance: Use Switzer as the default free stand-in whenever a brief asks for Helvetica, Inter or a clean Swiss sans and you cannot license the real thing — it has the full 100-900 range plus true italics, which Inter's free italics and most Google Sans options do not match. Load it as a variable font via the Fontshare CSS API (f[]=switzer@1,2 gives upright + italic variable) rather than pulling nine static weights, and self-host the woff2 if you need reproducible builds, since the CDN URLs under cdn.fontshare.com are opaque hashes that can rotate. The product page is a JS-only shell — query https://api.fontshare.com/v2/fonts?q=switzer for machine-readable style, axis, feature and language data.
why_it_matters: One of the very few free typefaces with a genuinely complete nine-weight range and matched italics, from a real foundry, under a licence that clears commercial work — it removes the usual excuse for shipping system-ui.
notable_for: ITF Free Font License, commercial use allowed
queryable via the public Fontshare API
